question: Does the wili_100k_500 stored release model reproduce under the UNPATCHED fp32 spm_train it was trained with? If it does, the 107-language gate FAIL against the fp64 retrain is a trainer-build numerical effect rather than a defect in the stored model.

provenance.note: provenance()'s 'retrained_*' keys describe fp32null; the fp64 container's size and mtime are under models.fp64

fp32null_provenance.spm_train_build: UNPATCHED fp32: cimeister/sentencepiece 2b7ec9b8e86a61f7772236471f948850872d8918, the parent of d0208d9; c5921a2 also absent
fp32null_provenance.trainer_code: UNILID 0.3.0, identical to the fp64 arm

training_corpus.manifest_definition: sha256 of the newline-joined 'name:size:sha256' lines of the per-language files in sorted name order
training_corpus.identity_with_published_training_corpus: ASSUMED, not verified. Evidence: the GitHub release supplies the WiLI corpus and the WiLI-2018 train/test split is deterministic (fixed x_train/y_train files, not resampled). No record ties the released models to these exact bytes.

row_alignment: by language name (langs.index), never by position

stored_vs_fp64.method: ordered token list from the container's base tokenizer

stored_vs_fp32null.method: ordered token list from the container's base tokenizer

threshold_provenance.calibrated_on: the GlotLID-C base model, comparing retrains produced by the SAME trainer build; the only benign source of variance there was a different subsampling draw of the same corpus
threshold_provenance.applied_to: all three arms identically, so the failing sets compare like for like
threshold_provenance.benign_variance_of_arms_a_and_o: not measured. Both cross the pre-0.3.0 / 0.3.0 trainer-version change; only arm (b) is within a single trainer version.

what_arm_a_does_and_does_not_establish.null_arm_for: the spm_train BUILD only. The fp32null retrain holds the trainer code, corpus, base tokenizer and CLI flags fixed against the fp64 arm and changes only the binary.
what_arm_a_does_and_does_not_establish.if_arm_a_fails: the fp32 -> patched fp64 spm_train change is not what makes the fp64 retrain differ from the transformed stored model. Arm (b) then measures how much the build DOES account for.
what_arm_a_does_and_does_not_establish.what_it_still_does_not_establish: that the difference lies in the stored model. The fp32null retrain runs UNILID 0.3.0 while the stored model was produced by pre-0.3.0 code, so arms (a) and (o) both still cross the trainer-version change. Attributing the residual to the stored model assumes analysis/correct_special_token_mass.correct undoes the ONLY pre-0.3.0/0.3.0 difference that reaches a row. This run does not test that assumption.

non_gating_columns.note: mass_weighted_diff_retrain_weighted keeps the name it has in analysis/gate_correction.py, where the numerator side was always a retrain. Here it means the same sum weighted by the NUMERATOR row's probabilities, whatever that side is in the arm; in arm (b) neither side is a transform.

a.comparison: fp32 null arm: fp32null retrain vs transformed stored model
a.delta_definition: fp32null minus transformed stored, over real tokens

b.comparison: pure build effect: fp64 retrain vs fp32null retrain (both on the corrected scale; no transformation involved)
b.delta_definition: fp64 minus fp32null, over real tokens

o.comparison: the original gate: fp64 retrain vs transformed stored model
o.delta_definition: fp64 minus transformed stored, over real tokens

signed_mean_correlation_across_arms.these_are_not_independent: signed_mean_o == signed_mean_a + signed_mean_b exactly, so cov(a,o) = var(a) + cov(a,b). a_vs_o approaches 1 whenever var(a) dominates var(b), which it does here; the correlation is therefore a restatement of the magnitude comparison, not separate evidence for it.

script_breakdown.method: share of letters in the language's own training file whose Unicode name starts with LATIN, over the first 200,000 characters; Latin iff >= 0.5

corpus_identity_check.claim: every wili_corpus_shared/<lang>_train.txt is exactly the lines of the released WiLI-2018 x_train.txt carrying that y_train label, in order
corpus_identity_check.what_this_does_not_establish: that the PUBLISHED model was trained on these bytes. It establishes only that the retrains' corpus is the released WiLI-2018 training split verbatim.

upstream_sentence_cap_split.pipeline_setting: the retrains pass max_sentence_length=1000000; sentencepiece's upstream default is 4192
upstream_sentence_cap_split.status: CANDIDATE CAUSE, NOT MEASURED. No record states what max_sentence_length the published run used, and no run at the default has been performed.
upstream_sentence_cap_split.separation: 0 of the languages that PASS arm (a) have an over-cap line; 65 of the failing ones do. The split is one-sided, but 41 languages fail arm (a) with no over-cap line at all, so the cap cannot be the whole explanation.

floor_decomposition.floor_definition: a real token is on the floor when its log-prob is within 1e-06 nats of the row's minimum
floor_decomposition.floor_is_set_by_corpus_size: measured by experiment B0 on 2026-08-17 (outputs/rerelease/plateau_vs_corpus_size.json): within a fixed language the floor falls about 2.19 nats per decade of training tokens, R-squared 0.999

wili_test_cells.note_macro_fpr_is_not_independent: WiLI-2018 test is balanced (500 items per label), so every label has n - support = 117,000 and macro FPR = total errors / (235 * 117,000), a deterministic function of accuracy. Verified per row above.

produced_by: scratchpad/fp32null_verdict.py (the three arms and their cross-checks)
scratchpad/fp32null_augment.py (corpus check, floor decomposition, upstream sentence-cap split, WiLI test cells)
